description: We’re a team from Arequipa, Peru. Our name joins hanan, the upper world of the Andean cosmovision, with qocha, the high-altitude lagoon. That’s exactly where our project lives.
summary: Hanan Qocha is a decision support tool for high Andean farms in the Salinas and Aguada Blanca Reserve (Arequipa, Peru). It compares farm management strategies, including adding cushuro (Nostoc sphaericum), an iron and protein rich cyanobacterium that grows wild in wetland ponds "cochas" and has never been managed. It combines three sources: NASA satellite data (HLS, SMAP, ECOSTRESS, POWER, SRTM) to find suitable ponds; Qocha Ñawi, our in-situ water quality sensor: and Qocha Twin, a digital twin with computer vision that forecasts growth and tells growers when and how much to harvest. Strategies re rank with the grower's priorities like water, income, soil, etc. Under rainfall and temperature scenarios, always showing evidence, information gaps and risks. It matters because 43.2% of rural children in Peru live with anemia, and iron supplements and fresh meat rarely reach the highlands.
details:
. Value proposition and benefits. Hanan Qocha turns a wild, unmanaged, iron-rich food into a decision a grower can plan. With NASA data it tells a high-Andean producer where cushuro ponds suit, how the water is now, and when and how much to harvest, and it compares farm strategies by the grower's own priorities. Benefits: local iron without cold chains, planned harvests, less over-harvesting, and honest uncertainty.

2. NASA data and how we apply it. HLS v2.0: NDWI and NDVI to find water and wetland vegetation. SMAP SPL3SMP_E: soil moisture, checked by our sensor. ECOSTRESS ECO_L2T_LSTE: surface temperature. NASA POWER: rain, temperature and radiation per pond, driving the scenario sliders. SRTM: elevation and slope. Earthdata CMR: data discovery. Everything is harmonised per pond and farm into the Cushuro Suitability Index (IAC = 0.4 satellite + 0.4 in situ + 0.2 vision).

3. Process diagram. Satellite data, the Qocha Ñawi sensor and a pond camera feed Qocha Twin, which computes the IAC and returns harvest decisions, pond management and a farm strategy. Photos recalibrate the model each season.

4. Progress and evidence. Published web app with map, pond sheets, twin with sliders, and strategy comparer. Real satellite data processed: 120 HLS readings, 16 SMAP passes, 33 ECOSTRESS scenes, 681 days of POWER per site, 6 ponds. The built Qocha Ñawi device with its 3D models. Colony segmentation on pond photos. Automated data checks on every change. Pond sheets, sensor readings and photos shown in the app demo are simulated.

5. Impact in the area. Pilot: three farms in the Salinas and Aguada Blanca National Reserve (Arequipa). Intended impact: a managed local source of iron and protein, extra rainy-season income, and decisions that support, never replace, the producer. Rural child anemia in Peru is 43.2% (ENDES 2025). Illustrative estimate: 30.9 kg of dry cushuro at the low end of reported iron (15.7 mg/100 g dry) gives about 4.9 g of iron, like roughly 194 kg of beef at 25 mg/kg. Local iron content still needs measuring.

6. Field visits. Three visits (20 October, 27 October, 10 November 2026): water-quality measurements with portable instruments, pond photos and talks with producers. They set the model ranges, the segmentation photos and the wording of recommendations.

7. Use of AI. Claude and Claude Code (Anthropic) for code, data analysis, scripts, writing and translation; a local Whisper model only to align narration with video. The app itself uses no machine-learning model: logistic growth and classical OpenCV segmentation.

8. Institutions. UNSA and UNI. Data: NASA, ESA/Copernicus, Esri.

9. Sources. Corpus-Gomez et al. (2021), Agroindustrial Science 11(2); INEI, ENDES 2025; Nostoc studies: https://rsdjournal.org/index.php/rsd/article/view/34391, https://repositorio.upch.edu.pe/handle/20.500.12866/18422, Mouga et al. (2024), Biology, https://www.mdpi.com/2079-7737/13/5/306/htm; challenge page: https://www.spaceappschallenge.org/2026/challenges/adapting-farms-with-nasa-data/
